l.i: Quæ Planci auspiciis mœnia struêta ferunt.

main_text.l: Lentus Arar placidi fluminis addit aquas:
hem diuitiis longo iam tempore notam,
(Hen quam diuitibus non licet esse pius)
c me facta patrum nafrare nefanda necesse est.

l.i: Vnum pro multis sat memorare scelus.

main_text.l: c nuper Christi felici de grege raptas

l.i: Vna, heu, quinas flamma vorauit oves:

main_text.l: dit & ingemuit Pietas, & fertur ab alto
Tales cana Fides ore dedisse sonos:

l.i: Hoc etenim, hoc ardent viscepa nostro rogo.

main_text.l: ama volat, sanctoque celer depascitur artus,

l.i: Nempe ut supplicij sit breuitate leuis.

main_text.l: nibus in mediis (mihi credite vera loquuto,
Sic faueant cœli numina dextra mihi)

l.i: Et Christum tituhas lingua sonabat adhuc:

main_text.l: uum paterex alto charos miseratus alumnos

l.i: Hac ad se, exutos corpore, voce vocat,

main_text.l: os (ait) ô anima, cœli germana propago,

page.notes: Printed text is a fragmentary, damaged verse page: the left edge of each line is cropped, and the first letters of many lines are lost. Readings such as "hem", "is", "c", "ota", "tando", "ama", "nibus", "ctora", "uum", "os" are fragments of words cut off by the scan edge, and the restored letters are not certain. Several long-s and ligature letters (s, ꝑ-type forms) were read as plain letters; "Sndis", "Ioan" and similar forms are approximations. Lines with italic type were transcribed in italics as seen; the Greek-looking mark "&" stands for the printed et-sign. Verse layout per line is retained; the original line ends may not match exactly due to the cropped edge.
